subject: Accelerated VM evidence & SLA acceptance for SIG/CORP audit
messages:
From: Claire Zhang <claire@fintechcorp.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai; priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: security+vuln@fintechcorp.com
Date: Tue, 13 May 2025 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: evidence package + CVE SLO attestation for SIG review

Hi Soojin / Priyom,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. As we prepare FinTech Corp's SIG submission for next week, we need a compact evidence packet documenting Redwood's current vulnerability management posture. Specifically we need: 

- A single archive with scan exports covering the last 30 days (open/closed findings).
- A one-page attestation describing target SLAs for CVE remediation (Critical/High/Medium), and the process for exceptions.
- A short note on scan cadence (internal infra vs. 3rd-party libs) and how you track regressions.
- Any proof that critical CVEs reported in the last 90 days were triaged and closed (CVE IDs if possible).

Can you confirm by EOD PT whether you can provide these artifacts? Also looping in our auditor Ben (3rd-party) in case he has format preferences.

Claire Zhang
Security Program Manager
FinTech Corp

P.S. If you have a signed SLA mapping or commit letter we can attach to the SIG MAT, that would be ideal.

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhang <claire@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, Ben Alvarez <ben.alvarez@3rdparty-audit.com>
Date: Tue, 13 May 2025 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: evidence package + CVE SLO attestation for SIG review

Hi Claire —

Appreciate the clear list. We've compiled a compact evidence package and attached the key artifacts to this thread (see attachments). Quick summary in-line: 

- Scan archives: vm-scan-full-2025-05-01-to-2025-05-10.zip contains exports from our authenticated network scans and container image scans; each export includes timestamps and file hashes.

- Attestation / SLA summary (cve-remediation-commitments-2025-05.pdf):
  * Critical (P1/Critical): target remediation or compensating control within 7 calendar days from detection; emergency patch window and rolling rollback plan documented.
  * High (P2): target 30 calendar days to remediate, with weekly progress updates tracked in our ticketing system.
  * Medium/Low: target 90 calendar days with risk-accepted exceptions documented and reviewed quarterly.

- Scan cadence: authenticated network & host scans run weekly; container image scans run on every image push and daily for pinned registries; dependency/software composition scans run nightly against npm/pypi/maven manifests. Third-party library MB vulnerability snapshots are updated weekly and exceptions are recorded in thirdparty-exceptions-2025-05.csv.

- Recent CVE closure evidence: the attached PDF includes a short table listing CVE-2025-1234 (closed 2025-04-29), CVE-2025-2108 (mitigated via config change 2025-04-12), and CVE-2025-3170 (backported patch 2025-03-21). Each line references the internal ticket ID and the scan finding export row.

Notes & caveats:
- For third-party managed services we provide documented exception workflows; where vendor patches are required we include expected vendor ETA and compensating controls.
- We do not attach full binary scan logs to outbound requests for security reasons; the archive contains sanitized exports and hashes so FinTech can validate ingestion.

If this looks good, please confirm and we'll produce a single signed attestation page for the SIG MAT with an authorized signer (security lead). Happy to walk Ben through the archive if he prefers a short review call.

Thanks,

Soojin Lee
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachment: vm-scan-full-2025-05-01-to-2025-05-10.zip; cve-remediation-commitments-2025-05.pdf; thirdparty-exceptions-2025-05.csv

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 08:15:40 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: evidence package + CVE SLO attestation for SIG review

Claire —

Quick operational addendum to Soojin's note:

- Ticketing & tracking: All VM findings are tracked in our internal system (RED-SEC-####). We maintain an automated mapping from scanner finding ID -> ticket -> remediation PR/patch. Weekly exports include the mapping column.

- SLA exceptions: The CSV lists active exceptions with a short rationale and compensating control. Exceptions are approved by the Security Ops manager and reviewed quarterly by the Risk team.

- Regression detection: We run baseline differential scans for containers and infra; any re-opened finding is auto-prioritized one level higher for triage. Historical deltas are included in the archive under /deltas/2025-04-30_to_2025-05-10/.

If you need the attestation signed by our CISO for the SIG MAT, we can get a signature-ready page by EOD Thu (15 May).

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai
